actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.name: ticks

inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

device.name: ACT bimanual ViperX insertion scene (MuJoCo model)

facts.text: The insertion scene is the MJCF file bimanual_viperx_insertion.xml; its root element is <mujoco> and it includes scene.xml and vx300s_dependencies.xml
The scene includes the left and right ViperX arm bodies from vx300s_left.xml and vx300s_right.xml
The scene adds a free peg body and a free socket body, each with a free joint

The actuator section lists a position actuator for the six joints and two finger slides of each arm; the control ranges are waist +-3.14158, shoulder -1.85005 to 1.25664, elbow -1.76278 to 1.6057, forearm_roll +-3.14158, wrist_angle -1.8675 to 2.23402, wrist_rotate +-3.14158, left_finger 0.021 to 0.057 and right_finger -0.057 to -0.021
The keyframe stores 30 qpos values: the 16 arm and finger values, seven for the peg and seven for the socket
The upstream joint-space insertion environment loads bimanual_viperx_insertion.xml
The upstream control timestep is DT = 0.02 s
The insertion environment is built with control_timestep=DT and time_limit=20
The upstream joint-space action is 14 values: six left arm joints, one left gripper, six right arm joints and one right gripper
The task expands each normalized gripper action into two finger control values before stepping the model
The insertion task initialises qpos[:16] to START_ARM_POSE and copies START_ARM_POSE into data.ctrl
START_ARM_POSE has 16 values, eight per arm
The only <option> in the scene is commented out, so the model sets no active integration timestep
The end-effector insertion scene has only the four finger actuators
The end-effector task drives the arms through mocap positions and quaternions and writes only four gripper values to data.ctrl

determinism.notes: MuJoCo integrates one model deterministically from one initial state; the bridge resets to the model defaults and its cap.world.reset.v1 seed input is not used, so a run repeats exactly on the same engine but no seed selects a different trajectory

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it reads the include-expanded MJCF for the actuator control ranges and the joint dimensions but integrates a placeholder first-order motion of each actuated joint toward its control target, so contacts, mesh geometry, actuator dynamics and the free peg and socket bodies are not MuJoCo's

the bridge exposes the raw 16-value actuator ctrl and the model's qpos/qvel; the upstream joint-space task takes a 14-value action and expands each gripper to two finger positions (sim_env.py:58-71), sets START_ARM_POSE and BOX_POSE on reset (sim_env.py:180-183), and adds the task reward, camera images and 20 s time limit (sim_env.py:48); that task layer is not served
the model sets no active <option timestep> (assets/scene.xml:2 is commented out), so the integration step is the engine's default; the fake uses a placeholder step, not a model fact
MuJoCo itself was not importable where the gate ran, so no trajectory of this package was compared with the real engine
the fake does not load the STL meshes or resolve contacts, equality constraints or tendons
no physical ViperX or ALOHA robot is modelled and nothing was validated against hardware

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the integration state is kept and stays readable
